summary.title: Roguelike Tutorial in Rust + tcod
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a roguelike game in Rust using the libtcod library, following a 13-part tutorial ported from the Python original.
takeaways: Roguelike games can be built in Rust with the libtcod library, which handles ASCII grid rendering, input, path finding, field of view and noise.
The tutorial is split into 13 parts covering graphics, map and dungeon generation, FOV, combat, GUI, items, spells, saving and character progression.
The port avoids global variables and Python-style backreferences, storing game objects in a Vec and passing references instead.
The author suggests using the tutorial to learn concepts, then starting fresh with your own game design.
summary.summary: This is a Rust port of the Complete Roguelike Tutorial, which originally used Python and libtcod. It explains why Rust and libtcod were chosen, and lists the alternatives T-Engine and rot.js. It also describes how the port differs from the original: no globals, a Vec-based object store instead of backreferences, and a single source file. The bulk of the page is a 13-part outline, from setting up the screen and moving an @ character through to equipment bonuses.
